page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-24-lssd is an instance in the Network Optimized family. It is equipped with 24 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 processor architecture and provides 90 GB of system memory, which yields an allocation of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server bundles 1611 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage across four drives, while containing no hardware GPU accelerators.

The hardware configuration emphasizes local storage performance and dedicated processing consistency. By integrating 1611 GB of NVMe SSD capacity directly on the host, primary read and write operations operate without network storage layer overhead. In addition, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures that compute resources are fully provisioned to the tenant rather than shared via burstable scheduling pools. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned to the instance.

From an efficiency perspective, the bundling of high-capacity local NVMe storage reduces reliance on external block storage arrays for high-throughput read/write pipelines. The balance between 24 cores, 90 GB of memory, and fast local NVMe capacity positions the instance for high-I/O operations, including transactional databases, operational data stores, distributed caching layers, and network services that demand low local data access latency.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-24-lssd is a network-optimized virtual server instance configured with 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 90 GB of RAM, representing 3.75 GB of memory per core. The configuration bundles 1611 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across four drives, while omitting discrete GPU accelerators. The compute resources operate on dedicated allocation, providing stable processing capacity without multi-tenant CPU contention. By pairing a balanced compute-to-memory ratio with directly attached NVMe media, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for architectures that require fast local disk operations alongside multi-threaded execution, eliminating separate network block storage overhead. The c4n-standard-24-lssd is engineered for high-throughput transactional databases, data processing pipelines, caching layers, and latency-sensitive network services requiring significant local storage capacity.
